output.myth: Varosk was the coat Ennu the Kite-Wright sewed for a fisher named Mot, from goat-gut and pine tar, so thick the sea ran off it like rain off a roof. Mot wore it into every squall and came home dry. Tavo saw this and was jealous, for nothing of his had ever kept anything dry. So one night he came down on the boat with his whole breath and Mot went over the rail. The coat held the sea out, and held it out, and held Mot in. Nobody bails a coat. The water stayed outside and the man stayed inside, and the coat carried him out past the last gull. Kael has cast for him every night since and never once caught him. Hesk counts the buttons and has not yet agreed the number is right. Mot is up there still, a little dry, looking for the way home.
output.verse:
Sea runs off the hood,
the man stays dry inside it.
Kael casts; he's not caught.

The right hem corner star 85162 (about x=360, y=377) sits on the inner edge of the right sleeve shape rather than on the outer hem corner, so the hem reads as narrower on the right than on the left.

The gold lines form a connect-the-dots triangle-like frame, not a copy of the silhouette, so that check passes. The blue silhouette is a real outline of a hooded coat with sleeves and is upright, with the hood at the top and the hem at the bottom.
